subject: chemistry_2
question_text: Give the oxidation states of halogens in the following: a) Cl₂O b) ClO₂⁻ c) KBrO₃ d) NaClO₄

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Cl₂O and ClO₂⁻
lines: Take oxygen as −2 and make the total equal
to the charge on the species.
steps.why: Oxygen is −2 in all of these compounds because it is more electronegative than any halogen except fluorine. The total then has to equal the charge on the species: zero for a neutral compound, −1 for the ClO₂⁻ ion. That single rule answers all four parts.
common_mistakes: Setting the total to zero for ClO₂⁻. It is an ion of charge −1, so the total must be −1.
Forgetting that Cl₂O has two chlorine atoms. 2x = +2 gives +1 for each chlorine, not +2.
steps.memory_tip: Oxygen −2, then make the sum equal the charge written on the species.
steps.margin_note: Show one line of working for each part. Bare answers are marked, but working protects you against an arithmetic slip.

steps.label: KBrO₃ and NaClO₄
lines: +5 and +7 with oxygen. Fluorine is the
steps.why: Potassium and sodium are always +1, so they enter the sum as a known number. The positive states arise only because the halogen is joined to oxygen, which is more electronegative than it. Fluorine is the most electronegative element of all and has no d orbitals, so it never takes a positive oxidation state; the +1, +3, +5, +7 series belongs to chlorine, bromine and iodine.
common_mistakes: Taking potassium or sodium as −1. Both are group 1 metals and are always +1 in their compounds.
Writing a positive oxidation state for fluorine in a similar question. Fluorine is only −1 in compounds and 0 in F₂.
steps.memory_tip: One more oxygen atom raises the halogen by two: +1, +3, +5, +7.
steps.margin_note: Write the four answers together on one line at the end. An examiner marking four short parts looks for them in one place.

insider_note: This is a four-part question worth two marks, so each part is about half a mark. Answer all four; three correct parts with long working scores less than four short ones.
